title: skills: five principle gaps the #9296 wave exposed in checklist-test / checklist-author / dogfood-verification
body:
Related to #9296. **Skills changes are ADR-class — draft PR, human merge, no auto-merge, no queue** (maintainer ruling 2026-08-11: 「所有 skills 的更新和 adr 类似，需要人工审核」). Companion card #9386 carries the `docs/qa/RUNNER.md` half, deliberately split so the platform facts are not held behind this review.

Filed under the 2026-08-12 filter that retired routine skill suggestions (「那些搞得后来 skills 越来越乱」): **only principle errors/gaps qualify.** Each entry below is a rule the skill states, a measurement showing it did not hold, and the smallest correction. Nothing here is a lesson-learned essay.

## 1. `checklist-test` / `checklist-author` mandate a subagent fleet neither can guarantee exists

**Stated**: checklist-test — 「派发 runner 子代理时，**必须用 `opus`**」. checklist-author — 「一轮全量 sweep ≈ 5 个 hunter + 8 个 writer agent」.

**Measured**: the R4 runner reported *no Task/subagent tool existed in its session*, so the five hunter angles and the per-area writers ran **sequentially, by one reader**. It declared the deviation unprompted — good instinct, but the skill never asked for it, so the next runner may not.

**Why it is a principle gap, not a nit**: SWEEP.md's entire claim is that different angles catch different miss classes **because the readers are independent**. A silent collapse to one reader leaves the findings intact but voids the *"nothing else was missed"* conclusion — and nothing in the output distinguishes the two.

**Correction**: state the fallback (run angles sequentially when no subagent tool is available) **and require the deviation to be declared in the report**, so a degraded sweep is never mistaken for a full one.

## 2. Neither skill says where the cost actually is — and it is not the test items

**Measured this wave, same 190-item ledger, same subject sha:**

| runner | environment | items completed | wall clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 (local subagent) | reused an already-provisioned tree | **18, round complete** | 39 min |
| R3-A (cloud) | cold container: clone → install → console build | ~15, then IDLE with 39 not-run | 150 min |
| R3-B (cloud) | cold container | 4 partial / 35 not-run | ~50 min |
| R3-C (cloud) | cold container | 13 | ~50 min |

The three cold containers burned ~**72M cache-read tokens** between them and left ~⅔ of their areas unrun; the warm local runner finished its round at roughly 4–5× the per-minute rate. Each cold container spent 20–40 minutes before its first verdict — install, the #9307 console-build ordering bug, a missing `packages/cli` dist, git-hook overrides.

**Correction**: checklist-test §2 currently says only 「整轮只构建一次」. It should say **one provisioned tree, reused across rounds**, and that a cold container per round is the dominant cost — justified only when a round must outlive the dispatching session (long browser runs, dogfood). This is the single largest cost lever in the skill and it is currently absent.

## 3. No skill states the cheapest ordering: pins first, in bulk

**Measured**: 77 of 190 active items carry an `automated.ref`. One vitest invocation over an area's 12 pinned files gave 91 tests in 80 s — evidence for 12 items from one command. RUNNER rule 6 says *don't re-prove what automation pins*, but nothing tells a runner to **do the pinned set first, batched per area**, before hand-driving anything.

**Correction**: add the tiering to checklist-test §1 — Tier 1 pinned (batch per area), Tier 2 unpinned P0/P1 (hand-drive), Tier 3 unpinned P2 (defer unless a change reaches them). On this ledger that is 77 / 62 / 47, i.e. the hand-driving load is **one third** of the item count, and the sweep's real value is concentrated there.

## 4. No definition of "done" for a round — so partial runs were filed as full ones

**Measured**: two run issues carry the title `(FULL area)` with bodies reading `0 PASS / 1 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL (10 not-run)` and `(11 not-run)`. A third round, told 「某个区跑不动就记 blocked，move on」, took that as licence to file a stub and stop. One runner *did* break the title convention on purpose — 「consulted 9 of 20 items, so claiming a full area would be false」 — which is the behaviour the skill should be requiring, not leaving to conscience.

**Correction**: an area is done only when **every** item has a verdict. A round that cannot finish files what it has **plus an explicit handoff list naming the unreached items**, and its title must state the consulted fraction. `not-run` is an honest verdict; `(FULL area)` over 11 not-run items is not.

## 5. ⚠️ No rule for access-control findings — and the omission caused a real disclosure

**What happened**: a dispatch prompt told runners to withhold an access-control reproduction from the public run issue and post it to the wave's tracking card "for the maintainer". The runner complied exactly. **The tracking card is also a public issue in a public repository**, so a working reproduction of an unauthenticated read/write hole was published. The runner flagged the doubt in its own report; the skill offered it no rule to follow.

`checklist-author` says security-sensitive findings are not filed publicly without the maintainer. **`checklist-test` — the skill that actually drives the app and is therefore the one that will find these — says nothing at all.**

**Correction**: add to checklist-test's Guardrails, in the same register as 「不伪造覆盖」:

> **Never publish a reproduction for an authentication or authorization hole anywhere on GitHub** — not the run issue, not a tracking card, not a comment. Record the item id, the clause, and `detail withheld pending maintainer`. Hold the reproduction in the session and stop. A finding whose existence is public but whose recipe is not is still a complete, actionable report; getting a defect fixed never requires handing anyone a working exploit.

## 6. One factual error to fix while in these files

`dogfood-verification` §1 documents `/api/v1/meta/app?id=<appId>` with a package-id example. The parameter keys on the app **name** (`showcase_app` / `setup` / `studio` / `account`); a package id returns `{"items":[]}`, which reads exactly like missing metadata. Same error appears in two checklist items (tracked in #9334) and as a fact in #9386.

## Scope discipline

⛔ Nothing else goes in. Not the card-scaffolding lesson (pm-dispatch, and the maintainer corrected it live). Not the `qa-run` sweep-exclusion (already assigned to the skills seat). No prose about "experience"; every entry above is a rule, a measurement, and a correction. Draft PR, human merge, and per the model-tiering rule this is **not** a mandatory-fable card — it touches `checklist-test` / `checklist-author` / `dogfood-verification`, not `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`.
